project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial from a branching caudex; leaves concentrated at the base; long mostly leafless peduncles each bear a yellow head; pappus consists of 5–7 aristate scales.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Natural Purola Plants lists Tetraneuris scaposa; Travis — UT herbarium index contains Tetraneuris scaposa var. scaposa; Williamson — dedicated county treatment of var. scaposa.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Canonical path remains tetraneuris-scaposa for stability; learner text teaches the accepted local variety var. scaposa.

morphology_keys.habit: Low rosette-forming plant with 1–many erect flowering stalks.
morphology_keys.leaves: Mostly basal/proximal, linear to oblanceolate or spatulate, entire or rarely toothed/lobed, often gland-dotted.
morphology_keys.heads: Yellow rays and yellow discs, usually one head per long peduncle.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Outer phyllaries 8–16; inner series shorter and more numerous.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Tetraneuris scaposa with two varieties; var. scaposa is the Central Texas learner concept documented in Hays, Travis, and Williamson. Hymenoxys scaposa is a synonym at species level.
look_here_first: Start with perennial rosette architecture. Tetraneuris scaposa var. scaposa is a perennial with basal linear leaves and long mostly leafless peduncles bearing solitary yellow heads. This contrasts strongly with annual T. linearifolia.

comparisons.key_distinctions: T. scaposa var. scaposa is the local perennial rosette/scape species; T. linearifolia is annual and stem-leaved. T. acaulis is a more northern/western Texas species and is not being treated as a target-zone native without exact county evidence.
